subject: Request: conditional SLA adjustment for content-filter timeouts & tool-call fallbacks
messages:
From: Julie Durand <julie.durand@blueharbor.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: 2025-07-11T19:04:00Z
Subject: Repeated production impact from content filter timeouts — request for SLA adjustment

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We saw repeated end-user failures in our chatbot flows between 2025-07-11T15:20:00-16:05:00 EDT (approx). Symptoms: rapid sequence of content-filter timeouts that triggered tool-call retries and caused structured-output validation to fail. The result was increased latency and ~18% of sessions returning fallback responses. This impacted our premium customers on the Payments onboarding flow.

We attached a small sample of filtered requests and logs (request_logs_20250711.zip) and a CSV with examples (filtered_examples_7-11.csv).

Given the impact on paid customers, we need Redwood to: 
- Acknowledge the incident window and provide a proposed SLA treatment (credit or exclusion) for filter-induced failures;
- Confirm an interim mitigation plan so this doesn't reoccur this week;
- Tell us whether content-filter timeouts and tool-call structured-output failures are covered under the existing latency uptime SLA or can be treated as an exception for that window.

Please treat this as high priority — our ops team is ready to provide more traces if useful.

Thanks,
Julie
VP Product, Blue Harbor
ops@blueharbor.com

--- attachment: request_logs_20250711.zip (log package, 2.4MB)
--- attachment: filtered_examples_7-11.csv (CSV, 8KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Julie Durand <julie.durand@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-11T19:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Repeated production impact from content filter timeouts — request for SLA adjustment

Hi Julie — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. We're prioritizing this.

Quick summary of what we'll do immediately:
1) Ingest the logs you attached and correlate to our filter metrics (already underway).
2) Propose a temporary SLA treatment for the 45-minute window you reported: Redwood is prepared to treat filter timeouts and tool-call structured-output failures occurring during that window as an eligible exception to the normal per-token latency SLA, pending verification of root cause.
3) Provide a written mitigation & hardening plan within 6 business hours and a credit proposal within 24 hours.

Two asks from your side to speed validation:
- Confirm the exact customer tenant IDs (or a few request IDs) that show the 18% session failure rate;
- If you have any correlating Cloud provider logs (LB timeouts, etc.), attach them.

I will loop Marissa and Soojin on the engineering plan.

—Sean
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

> On 2025-07-11 19:04, Julie Durand wrote:
> > We saw repeated end-user failures...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-11T20:10:00Z
Subject: FW: Repeated production impact from content filter timeouts — preliminary RCA and mitigation options (internal)

Internal notes / preliminary RCA: we are seeing a short burst of unusually large multipart payloads with nested attachments that caused the content-filter queue to backlog. The backlog led to cascading retries at the tool-call layer and then to structured-output validation lapses when partial filter responses arrived.

Prelim timeline:
- 15:17:00 EDT: spike in payload size / attachments starts for tenant BH-Prime;
- 15:23:00: filter worker pool reaches 94% busy, queue times spike;
- 15:30:00: tool-call retries increase 4x;
- 16:02:00: first customer-visible fallback reported.

Suggested mitigation (short term):
- Increase filter concurrency for the affected region for 24 hours;
- Apply a fast-path rule to bypass heavyweight inspection for trusted tenants (BH-Prime) on low-risk endpoints;
- Add a conservative backoff at tool-call layer to prevent retry storms.

SLA treatment proposal (internal draft):
- Exclude filter timeouts and tool-call structured-output failures from per-token latency SLA for the window 2025-07-11T19:17:00Z — 2025-07-11T20:05:00Z while we verify;
- Offer a pro-rated credit of 10% of that day's consumption for the impacted tenant(s) as a gesture until fully validated.

I'll prepare a short ops timeline doc and a redline for legal once we agree on wording.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--- attachment: bh-incident-timeline-7-11.pdf (incident timeline, 120KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-11T21:05:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Repeated production impact from content filter timeouts — wording for exception request

Marissa / Sean — drafting proposed customer-facing language for the exception and mitigation plan. Suggest the following short paragraph for the SLA amendment request:

"For the incident window starting 2025-07-11T19:17:00Z and ending 2025-07-11T20:05:00Z, Redwood will treat content-filter timeouts and tool-call failures that lead to structured-output validation errors as an operational exception. These events will be excluded from per-token latency calculations for the purpose of SLA adjudication while Redwood completes investigation and implements the agreed mitigations."

I'll also add the proposed 10% day credit and the short-term configuration steps. Once Sean approves, we should send formally to Julie and loop legal for sign-off.

—Soojin
Sr. Product Manager, Runtime
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Julie Durand <julie.durand@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-12T01:15:00Z
Subject: Proposed SLA treatment & short-term mitigation for July 11 filter timeouts

Hi Julie — following our internal triage, here is the proposed course of action for Blue Harbor (BH-Prime tenant):

1) Incident acknowledgement: Redwood confirms the incident window 2025-07-11T19:17:00Z — 2025-07-11T20:05:00Z (UTC). The trigger was a spike in large multipart payloads to the content-filter pipeline that produced queue backpressure and caused tool-call retry storms.

2) SLA treatment: 
- During the stated window, content-filter timeouts and correlated tool-call structured-output failures will be treated as an operational exception and excluded from per-token latency SLA adjudication.
- Redwood will extend a pro-rated credit equal to 10% of the impacted tenant's bill for 2025-07-11 as an interim remedy; final credit will be confirmed after log reconciliation.

3) Short-term mitigation steps completed within 2 hours of this notice: 
- Increased filter worker concurrency for BH region;
- Deployed fast-path inspection rule for BH-Prime on the Payments endpoint;
- Added conservative retry/backoff at tool-call layer to limit cascading failures.

4) Next steps: 
- We will deliver a full RCA and final credit calculation within 24 business hours;
- If you accept the exception language above, we will route the wording to Legal for an SLA amendment addendum and send you the draft for signature.

Please confirm if you accept the proposed exception + credit and whether you want the addendum signed. If you prefer an alternate remediation (larger credit or other remedy), let us know and we will escalate to Commercial.

Best,
Sean
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

--- attachments: bh-incident-timeline-7-11.pdf (timeline), request_logs_20250711.zip (customer logs)
--- related link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9821

From: Julie Durand <julie.durand@blueharbor.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: 2025-07-12T03:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA treatment & short-term mitigation for July 11 filter timeouts

Sean — confirmed. We accept the exception as written and appreciate the 10% interim credit. Please route the SLA addendum to legal and copy our counsel (legal@blueharbor.com).

Two quick asks:
- Can you include in the RCA whether the new fast-path rule could change detection characteristics for other endpoints?
- We'll expect the final credit reconciliation within 24 business hours.

Thanks for the rapid response.

Julie
VP Product, Blue Harbor
julie.durand@blueharbor.com
ops@blueharbor.com
